description: This pattern occurs when a distributed system node acknowledges a state change (vote, accept, prepare) to its peers before ensuring that the state change is durable on stable storage. In Crash Fault Tolerant (CFT) protocols, this creates a window of vulnerability where a node "forgets" its vote upon restart. If the vote was pivotal in reaching a quorum, the system loses the quorum intersection guarantee. A new leader/recovery process can then form a new quorum that does not include the previous decision, leading to committed data being overwritten.
trigger_condition: High-concurrency environments where network latency is lower than disk latency, followed immediately by a node crash.
test_template: 1.  **Setup**: Initialize a cluster of size $N$ (where $Q$ is the quorum size).
